Issues.Title: fix(compiler): handle void expressions in constant literals
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

A template like `{{ [void 0, 1][1] }}` or `{{ {a: void 0}.a }}` fails to compile with `PureFunctionConstant does not handle expressions of type VoidExpr`. Constant literals get pooled through `GenericKeyFn.keyOf`, which handles `TypeofExpr` but has no case for `VoidExpr`.

Issue Number: #71867

## What is the new behavior?

`keyOf` builds a key for `VoidExpr` the same way it does for `TypeofExpr`, so these literals compile and get pooled.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler): handle void expressions in constant literals" (#71868)

Issues.Title: compiler: `void` inside a constant array or object literal throws in `PureFunctionConstant.keyOf`
Issues.Body:
In `@angular/compiler` 22.2.5, compiling a template with an array or object literal whose entries are all constants and include a `void` expression throws an unhandled error in both AOT and JIT compilation.

```js
import '@angular/compiler';
import { ɵcompileComponent } from '@angular/core';

class App {}
ɵcompileComponent(App, { template: '{{ [void 0, 1][1] }}' }); // or '{{ { a: void 0 }.a }}'
console.log(App.ɵcmp);
```

Compiling this template throws:

```
Error: PureFunctionConstant does not handle expressions of type VoidExpr
    at PureFunctionConstant.keyOf (@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:2334:13)
    at ConstantPool.getSharedConstant (@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:2264:21)
```

It should compile without error and pool the constant literal, just as it does for `{{ [typeof 0, 1][1] }}` or `{{ [!true, 1][1] }}`. The `void` operator is supported in template expressions, but `GenericKeyFn.keyOf` is missing a case for `VoidExpr` alongside `TypeofExpr`.

Credit: https://ucsbplse.github.io/
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "compiler: `void` inside a constant array or object literal throws in `PureFunctionConstant.keyOf`" (#71867)

Issues.Title: fix(router): do not call history.go() on first navigation after reload with canceledNavigationResolution 'computed'
Issues.Body:
With canceledNavigationResolution set to 'computed', cancelling the first navigation after a page reload called history.go() with a stale page id and moved the browser to an unrelated history entry. The router started with currentPageId 0 while the restored entry still carried the previous app instance's page id, so the computed delta was non-zero even though there was no previously activated page to go back to.

This differs from #71856: that PR synced currentPageId from the target entry on every NavigationStart while no navigation had succeeded. This PR instead initializes currentPageId once from the restored state at construction, so it tracks the page the router actually starts on, and a later popstate or eager navigation before any success cannot overwrite it. It also resets the browser url to the router's current url when a navigation is cancelled before any navigation has succeeded, so the browser does not stay on a route the router never activated.

Fixes #71849
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(router): do not call history.go() on first navigation after reload with canceledNavigationResolution 'computed'" (#71866)

Issues.Title: language-server: project reload loop and OOM with a deleted open TS file and solution-style external template (22.2.0)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a bug report or a feature request?

- [x] Bug Report
- [ ] Feature Request

### Summary

Angular Language Service 22.2.0 entered a self-sustaining project-reload/diagnostics loop in a multi-root Nx workspace. A TypeScript file had been deleted on disk while its editor remained open, and an external Angular component template from a different worktree was also open. The server repeatedly failed to find the deleted file's configured project, reloaded/re-analyzed the template's library project roughly every 1–2 seconds, and eventually aborted with a JavaScript heap OOM near 4 GB.

Closing the two editors associated with the deleted path (ordinary editor and Git diff), then running **Angular: Restart Angular Language server**, stopped the loop without reloading VS Code. The external template remained open and its language features worked afterwards.

### Please provide the steps to reproduce the issue [Bug Report only]

**Observed sequence in the affected workspace; not yet independently reproduced in a standalone minimal project:**

1. Open an Nx monorepo in VS Code with multiple linked worktree folders in one multi-root window.
2. Keep an external `.component.html` template open in a library whose `tsconfig.json` is solution-style (`files: []` with references to the library/spec configs). Its sibling component TypeScript editor is not open.
3. Have a TypeScript editor open in another worktree, then delete that TypeScript file on disk while leaving its editor open. In the observed incident, both its ordinary editor and Git diff remained open.
4. The server repeatedly logs `No config file` for the deleted path, interleaved with repeated enabling of the template library project.
5. Within approximately 43–60 seconds per process lifetime, the heap reaches approximately 4 GB and the server aborts. Automatic restarts repeat the same sequence until the language client gives up after five crashes in three minutes.

There is no public minimal reproduction yet; the original workspace is private. The path names and layout below are anonymized. These steps describe the observed state and sequence, not a confirmed universal reproducer.

### Please provide the expected behavior vs the actual behavior you encountered [Bug Report only]

**Expected:** An editor whose file was removed from disk should not cause repeated teardown/recreation and full Angular analysis of another open template's configured project. The server should settle and continue providing template features.

**Actual:** The same project-loading messages repeat about once per second, including repeated `No config file` errors for the deleted TS path. The server exhausts its heap, restarts, and eventually stops restarting. Template diagnostics/navigation become unavailable.

**Recovery observed:** Close only the saved editors for the deleted path, then restart the Angular language server. With the same workspace folders and external template still open, the log settled after about eight seconds. The replacement process remained alive for more than four minutes at approximately 1.4 GB RSS, with no further missing-file messages or crash. Template-to-component navigation was manually verified. This is current-session recovery, not evidence of permanent prevention.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw [Bug Report only]

Representative excerpt, with paths anonymized:

```text
[Info  - 19:44:51] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-a/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Error - 19:44:51] No config file for /workspace/worktree-a/libs/backend/src/deleted-file.ts
[Info  - 19:44:51] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Info  - 19:44:51] Enabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/libs/frontend/shared/tsconfig.lib.json.
[Info  - 19:44:52] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-a/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Error - 19:44:52] No config file for /workspace/worktree-a/libs/backend/src/deleted-file.ts
[Info  - 19:44:53] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Info  - 19:44:53] Enabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/libs/frontend/shared/tsconfig.lib.json.

[3348:0x12800810000] 43091 ms: Scavenge 4014.9 (4071.5) -> 4002.6 (4083.2) MB, pooled: 0.0 MB, 4.70 / 0.00 ms (average mu = 0.527, current mu = 0.565) allocation failure;
[3348:0x12800810000] 43122 ms: Scavenge 4026.8 (4083.2) -> 4011.4 (4090.7) MB, pooled: 0.0 MB, 4.83 / 0.00 ms (average mu = 0.527, current mu = 0.565) allocation failure;

FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
[Error - 19:45:28] Server process exited with signal SIGABRT.
[Error - 19:45:28] The Angular Language Service server crashed 5 times in the last 3 minutes. The server will not be restarted. See the output for more information.
```

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.145.0
- OS: macOS 26.6.2, arm64
- Extension: `angular.ng-template` 22.2.0
- Loaded `@angular/language-service`: 22.2.0
- Loaded `typescript/lib/tsserverlibrary`: 6.0.3
- Angular in the affected worktrees: 22.2.4. Other folders in the multi-root window use 21.2.10 and 22.1.8.
- Multi-root window: 35 linked worktree folders
- Server runtime: VS Code's `Code Helper (Plugin)` process
- `angular.server.useClientSideFileWatcher`: enabled (visible in the server arguments)

The same window/folder set was stable for approximately 20 minutes before the deleted-file error/reload loop began. Workspace size may amplify the cost, but does not by itself explain the transition into the continuous loop.

### Suspected mechanism (code-traced; not an isolated reproduction)

There appears to be an interaction between external-template project recovery and TypeScript project cleanup:

1. Project loading calls `enableLanguageServiceForProject`, which performs Angular analysis and `refreshDiagnostics()`.
2. A projects-updated event schedules diagnostics for open files.
3. For the deleted TypeScript file, `getDefaultProjectForScriptInfo` calls `openClientFile`, cannot find a configured project, and reports `No config file`.
4. TypeScript's open-client-file path also runs orphan project cleanup. A solution-style template's association established by `attachToComponentProject` may not be preserved by that cleanup.
5. Processing the still-open external template then calls `loadProjectForExternalTemplate` / `attachToComponentProject`, loading and analyzing the library project again and scheduling more diagnostics.

This is consistent with the repeated log sequence and the observed recovery, but **the exact heap-retention cause and causality of every internal step have not been independently established**.

The recovery methods are present in [14fbe04612](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/14fbe04612d29460c5d01d6c65cde579f0a42e95), which fixed #69768. This may be a relevant interaction/regression to investigate, not a claim that the commit alone is proven to cause the OOM.

An earlier log episode also showed repeated external-template project reloads and OOMs without a deleted-file error, so a deleted TS file may be one trigger rather than a necessary condition.

Related reports checked: #65356 and #65484 describe older language-service OOM incidents, but do not identify this particular solution-style template/project-reload sequence.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "language-server: project reload loop and OOM with a deleted open TS file and solution-style external template (22.2.0)" (#71864)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): add perf tracing to the preprocessor and ng-a…
Issues.Body:
…nalyze

Adds opt-in performance tracing to the preprocessor CLI and the Rust ng-analyze sidecar, controlled by three new flags:

  --perf-trace <path>     write a Chrome trace event JSON timeline
  --perf-summary <path>   write a per-phase summary JSON
  --perf-trace-detail     add per-query async slices and query keys

The trace can be opened in Perfetto or chrome://tracing. The Node driver records its compile phases, with an async slice per file so overlapping files show up correctly. ng-analyze records one slice per poll of each query on the real worker thread that ran it, with flow arrows from the cache miss that requested a query to where it starts executing. Both processes are merged into one file, with the Rust timestamps aligned to the Node clock.

The summary groups time by phase and by query kind (count, self, busy, queued and wall time, plus cache hits and counters like files parsed and filesystem reads), and is meant to be easy to feed into benchmark dashboards.

Tracing is off unless one of the flags is passed. The Rust tracing layer is only installed once an initialize asks for tracing, and each initialize turns recording on or off, so a long-lived sidecar can trace some runs and not others. The Node side uses a no-op tracer otherwise. With tracing off there was no measurable difference in compile time or memory on a compiler benchmark and on two real applications, and outputs were identical. With tracing on, wall time went up about 0.5-1.5% and peak memory about 3-6 MiB, with trace files around 1-2 MB for medium-sized targets.

This adds the tracing and tracing-subscriber crates to ng-analyze. tracing-subscriber is only used for non-wasm targets.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): add perf tracing to the preprocessor and ng-a…" (#71863)

Issues.Title: fix(router): do not call history.go() when cancelling navigation before first success
Issues.Body:
When the page reloads on an existing history entry with `canceledNavigationResolution: 'computed'`, `history.state` still carries the previous instance's `ɵrouterPageId`, while `HistoryStateManager.currentPageId` starts at `0` and is only updated on `NavigationEnd`. If a navigation is cancelled or errors before any navigation has succeeded (`lastSuccessfulId === -1`), `currentPageId` does not correspond to an activated route in the router, so `restoreHistory()` should not call `history.go()`.

Fixes #71849
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(router): do not call history.go() when cancelling navigation before first success" (#71862)

Issues.Title: fix(router): do not call history.go() on first navigation after reload with canceledNavigationResolution 'computed'
Issues.Body:
What broke: after a reload with `canceledNavigationResolution: 'computed'`, cancelling the first navigation called `history.go()` with a stale page id and moved the browser to the wrong history entry. The restored entry still carries the previous app instance's page id, while `HistoryStateManager` starts `currentPageId` at 0, so `restoreHistory()` computed a stale delta.

What changed: on `NavigationStart`, until the first navigation succeeds, `currentPageId` is aligned with the restored page id. History is left untouched when the first navigation is cancelled or errors. No-op when there is no restored state or the resolution is not `'computed'`.

How verified: two new tests in `computed_state_restoration.spec.ts` (guard rejection and resolver error on the first navigation after a reload) failed before the fix and pass after; full `//packages/router/test:test` passes (1255 specs, 0 failures).

Fixes #71849
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(router): do not call history.go() on first navigation after reload with canceledNavigationResolution 'computed'" (#71856)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): drop filesystem type parameter from preprocessor query engine
Issues.Body:
After routing module resolution, component resource resolution, and file
loading through `AnalysisHost`, the `Fs` type parameter on `QueryEngine`
and `QueryContext` no longer described any state the engine holds. It
survived only as a `PhantomData` marker, yet it still forced roughly a
hundred query, evaluator, analyzer, and compiler functions to carry a
`ResourceResolverFs + Clone + 'static` bound and kept the engine's types
tied to the filesystem implementation that hosts are meant to abstract
away.

Make `QueryEngine`, `QueryContext`, and the `QueryCtx` aliases concrete
types and remove the marker field, then drop the bound from every
function, method, and helper type that existed only to thread it
through, including the NgModule scope `ScopeEnv` and `Resolver`, the
streaming coordinator, and `DirtyFilesSnapshot`. The filesystem type now
appears only on the `new`, `new_with_options`, and `new_default`
constructors that wrap a filesystem and resolver in a `DefaultFsHost`, so
existing callers infer it as before, while `new_with_host` and
`new_default_with_host` accept any host directly. Tests that named
`QueryEngine<OverlayFileSystem>` now use the plain engine type, and
imports left unused by the removal are dropped.

Also reword the preprocessor contributor guideline on paths and module
resolution to describe the host boundary: analysis code resolves and
loads only through `AnalysisHost`, only host implementations touch a
filesystem or `oxc_resolver`, path arithmetic applies solely to
path-backed module IDs, and the TypeScript code-generation layer remains
a pure consumer of pre-resolved metadata. There is no change in
behavior.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): drop filesystem type parameter from preprocessor query engine" (#71860)

Issues.Title: fix(core): detect own NgZone by reference instead of instance ID
Issues.Body:
Previously, `NgZone` tracked instances with a module-local `ngZoneInstanceId` counter and
attached `isAngularZone_ID` / `isAngularZone_ID<n>` properties to each forked Angular zone.
`ChangeDetectionSchedulerImpl.shouldScheduleTick()` then checked `Zone.current.get(...)` for
that ID to decide whether a notification happened inside the app's own `NgZone` and could
skip hybrid change detection scheduling.

This breaks down in microfrontend setups where a host application and one or more separately
bundled Angular applications share a page and a global `Zone.js` instance. Because each
bundle has its own copy of `@angular/core`, every bundle starts its `ngZoneInstanceId`
counter at `0` and gets `isAngularZone_ID0`. If one zone-based application invokes a shared
service, callback, Observable, or event that notifies another application while running
inside the caller's `NgZone`, the receiving app's scheduler sees `isAngularZone_ID0` on
`Zone.current`, mistakes the foreign `NgZone` for its own, and skips scheduling change
detection — leaving its views un-updated even when the apps keep their `NgZone`s as siblings.

Instead of assigning per-bundle string IDs, `ChangeDetectionSchedulerImpl` now keeps a direct
reference to `ngZone._inner` and walks `Zone.current`'s `parent` chain checking
`zone === this.innerNgZone`. This preserves behavior for single-bundle multi-app setups and
child zones forked inside an app's `NgZone`, eliminates cross-bundle ID collisions, removes
module-level counter state and the exported `angularZoneInstanceIdProperty` symbol from
`ng_zone.ts`, and avoids string concatenation and property-map lookups on every notification.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(core): detect own NgZone by reference instead of instance ID" (#71859)

Issues.Title: docs: explain hydration errors from CDNs and browser extensions
Issues.Body:
Some CDN features and browser extensions change the HTML from the
server before hydration starts. These errors often happen only in
production or only for some users, so they are hard to find.

Prior to this commit, the docs didn't explain these causes and `NG0509`
had no error page.

With this change, the hydration guide explains these causes and their
fixes, and `NG0509` has an error page.

The `NG0509` code is now negative, like other codes that have an error
page. This changes the public API golden for `RuntimeErrorCode`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs: explain hydration errors from CDNs and browser extensions" (#71857)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): route preprocessor query engine I/O through AnalysisHost
Issues.Body:
Even with `AnalysisHost` and `DefaultFsHost` available, `QueryEngine`,
component resource loaders, and cross-file constant evaluation still held
a concrete filesystem and `oxc_resolver` instance and performed synchronous
file reads and specifier lookups directly. That prevented asynchronous,
filesystem-free bundler hosts from driving analysis and left synchronous
helper entry points able to bypass the host boundary.

Replace `fs` and `resolver` on `QueryEngine` with `Arc<dyn AnalysisHost>`,
retaining a temporary `PhantomData` marker for `Fs` so generic parameter
removal across query and evaluator signatures stays isolated to a separate
follow-up change. Existing constructors wrap `DefaultFsHost` to preserve
current behavior, while `new_with_host` and `new_default_with_host` allow
injecting custom asynchronous hosts directly.

Route file parsing, syntax-level static and dynamic dependency discovery,
ambient `.d.ts` scanning, local-compilation extra import checks, export-map
traversal, host-directive package resolution, and cross-file symbol chasing
through `AnalysisHost`, deleting the synchronous `resolve_specifier` helper
so future call sites cannot bypass the host. Convert Stage-1 and Stage-2
component `templateUrl` and `styleUrl` loading to asynchronous host calls
that concurrently resolve resources and static/dynamic module specifiers in
a single wave, fall back to `AnalysisHost::load` when inline resource text
is omitted, and exclude `external` modules from the program closure while
still reading their metadata on demand.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): route preprocessor query engine I/O through AnalysisHost" (#71855)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): introduce preprocessor analysis host trait and module ID interning
Issues.Body:
To let bundlers supply module resolutions, component resources, and file
contents asynchronously without exposing a filesystem to `ng-analyze`,
the query engine needs an abstract host boundary and a module identifier
representation that does not treat every ID as a filesystem path. Bundler
virtual module IDs (such as `\0`-prefixed Rollup IDs, Vite `/@id/...`
specifiers, or query-suffixed IDs) look like or contain path-like
segments that would be corrupted by structural path normalization or
platform case-folding.

Introduce the `host` module in `ng-analyze` defining `ModuleId`,
`IdKind` (`Path` vs `Virtual`), `ModuleFormat`, request/response records,
and the `AnalysisHost` trait for asynchronous `resolve`, `load`, and
`resolve_resource` operations. Provide `DefaultFsHost<Fs>` over
`oxc_resolver` and `ResourceResolverFs` as the synchronous filesystem
implementation that resolves futures immediately on first poll,
canonicalizes `rootDirs` backing paths, and delegates component resource
loading to `ResourceResolver`.

Extend `FileIdInterner` to store `(ModuleId, IdKind)` alongside each
`FileId`. Apply structural normalization and case-insensitive key
folding exclusively to `IdKind::Path` entries while storing and matching
`IdKind::Virtual` entries verbatim, and allow authoritative host
resolutions to override a previously defaulted `IdKind` on the same
`FileId` while keeping existing path-based callers unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): introduce preprocessor analysis host trait and module ID interning" (#71854)

Issues.Title: perf(compiler-cli): track ambient global consumers by name and cache .d.ts global names
Issues.Body:
> [!NOTE]
> Stacked on #71850. Only the last three commits are new.

With #71823, every file that looks up an ambient global depends on every `.d.ts` file in `tsconfig.json` `files`. Editing any of them re-analyzes every consumer, and rebuilding the index re-parses all of them. Every fresh analyzer also re-indexes them all, and a persistent build worker creates one analyzer per request.

This change:
1. Looks up an ambient global by scanning the `tsconfig.json` `files` `.d.ts` files in order, stopping at the first one that may declare it. That is the first file resolution would use anyway, so a global declared early in the list never reads the rest. Lookups from the start of the list are memoized per name.
2. Records the global names each consumer looks up, rather than making it depend on the files it scanned. An invalidated `.d.ts` keeps the names it declared. Before the next build, only that file is re-read, and only the consumers of names it started or stopped declaring are evicted.
   - A value change inside the same `.d.ts` (`declare const COMPILED: true` → `false`) leaves its names unchanged. The consumer still depends on that `.d.ts` directly, since it parsed it to evaluate the declaration, so the ordinary invalidation evicts it.
   - The diff and eviction run in `ensure_singletons_fresh`, before any per-file query reads the cache, rather than from within a lookup. Every entry point that reads per-file analysis calls it first: `run_coordinator` (batch, delta, and watch rebuilds), `analyze_file_wire_blocking`, and `analyze_file_semantic_blocking`.
   - The eviction also covers the whole-program singletons that read an evicted consumer. `ComponentMapping`, for example, evaluates `@NgModule.declarations` itself.
3. Caches the global names each `.d.ts` declares, per analyzer and across analyzers in the process, for as long as the file's text is unchanged. When the file already has a shared full parse, the names come from that parse.
4. Stops evicting the import graph and the whole-program singletons on an edit to a `.d.ts` that no query read except the ambient module index.

Emitted output doesn't change.

The tests cover:
- an unrelated `.d.ts` edit (nothing evicted, including the singletons)
- a lookup that stops early
- a new declaration that changes a lookup (consumer evicted only by `ensure_singletons_fresh`), including through `ComponentMapping`, a type-only candidate, and a global read through another file
- a value change (consumer evicted through its dependency on the `.d.ts`)
- a `.d.ts` that becomes readable
- reordering and inserting `tsconfig.json` `files`
- memoized lookups
- a `.d.ts` read by a query still evicting the singletons
- sharing names across analyzers

Optimized and local wire modes are both covered.

### Performance

Measured in-process with `ng-analyze` on 747 `.d.ts` files (6.0 MB, including `lib.dom.d.ts`, from `typescript`, `@types/node`, `rxjs`, `zone.js`, and `@angular/*`), symlinked like a Bazel execroot. The program is 11 `.ts` files that read `COMPILED` in `@Component` selectors and `@NgModule` declarations. Times are medians in milliseconds, optimized mode. Local mode is similar.

| Scenario | Before (#71850) | After | No ambient global read |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh analyzer (warm worker request), global declared in the first `.d.ts` | 56.7 | 4.0 | 3.7 |
| Fresh analyzer (warm worker request), global declared in the last `.d.ts`, or undeclared | 56.7 | 42.6 | 3.7 |
| A `.d.ts` touched with unchanged content, then a delta build | 49.9 | 0.1 | 0.1 |
| An unrelated `.d.ts` edited with a new declaration, then a delta build | 50.5 | 0.1 | 0.1 |

The first build in a new process is noisy. It is about the same as before when the lookup scans every file, and about 5 ms when the global is declared early. When a lookup scans every file, the remaining cost is opening and canonicalizing the `.d.ts` files, not parsing them.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "perf(compiler-cli): track ambient global consumers by name and cache .d.ts global names" (#71851)

Issues.Title: Router: with canceledNavigationResolution 'computed', cancelling the first navigation after a reload calls history.go() with a stale page id
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

With `canceledNavigationResolution: 'computed'`, cancelling (or erroring) the **first navigation after a page reload** makes the router call `history.go()` with a non-zero delta, so the browser jumps to an unrelated history entry instead of staying on the current one.

Cause (from `HistoryStateManager` in `_router-chunk.mjs`, 22.2.3):

- `currentPageId` starts at `0` in every new app instance.
- After a reload (or when the user comes back from another site via Back), `history.state` still carries the previous instance's `ɵrouterPageId` (for example `2`), and the initial navigation restores that state, so `browserPageId` returns `2`.
- If that initial navigation is cancelled (a guard returns `false`, a resolver errors, a `NavigationError` happens), `restoreHistory()` computes `targetPagePosition = this.currentPageId - this.browserPageId = 0 - 2` and calls `this.location.historyGo(-2)`.
- `lastSuccessfulId` is still `-1` at that point: there is no previous router-owned position to go back to, so any non-zero `historyGo` is wrong. If the first navigation keeps failing (e.g. a guard that rejects on startup), the app walks back through the history one batch at a time.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

No StackBlitz yet; minimal steps:

1. `provideRouter(routes, withRouterConfig({ canceledNavigationResolution: 'computed' }))` with routes `/a`, `/b`, `/c`, where `/c` has a `canActivate` guard that returns `false` when a flag (e.g. a `sessionStorage` key) is set.
2. Navigate in-app `/a` → `/b` → `/c`. `history.state.ɵrouterPageId` is now `2` on the `/c` entry.
3. Set the flag and reload the page on `/c`.

Expected: the cancelled initial navigation leaves the history position unchanged (at most resets the URL of the current entry).
Actual: the router calls `history.go(-2)` and the browser ends up on the entry before `/a`.

The same happens when the initial navigation fails for other reasons (startup error in a guard, a resolver throwing), and when the user returns with Back from another site to an entry that carries a page id.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
No exception; the browser silently navigates to another history entry (history.go(0 - restoredPageId)).
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular: 22.2.3 (router 22.2.3)
Browser: Chrome (latest stable)
```

### Anything else?

Possible fixes:
- When the initial navigation restores a state with `ɵrouterPageId`, initialize `currentPageId` from it (so `currentPageId - browserPageId === 0` until a navigation succeeds), or
- In `restoreHistory()` for `'computed'`, skip `historyGo` when no navigation has succeeded yet (`lastSuccessfulId === -1`) and only reset the URL of the current entry.

Our workaround is to never cancel the first navigation: guards return `NEVER` (hold the navigation) instead of `false`/`UrlTree` on startup failures, which is not obvious and changes first-navigation semantics.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Router: with canceledNavigationResolution 'computed', cancelling the first navigation after a reload calls history.go() with a stale page id" (#71849)

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [ ] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [x] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The `forRoot()`, `forChild()` and `PreloadAllModules` examples pass `ROUTES`, which is easy to mistake for the exported `ROUTES` injection token. Passing the token fails to compile, since these methods expect a `Routes` array.

Issue Number: #71837

## What is the new behavior?

The examples pass `routes`, the same name as the `routes` parameter documented below them.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Fixes #71837

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup
Issues.Body:
The karma builder schema documents the `poll` and `progress` options, but the application build it starts never receives them: `--no-progress` still logs build progress and `poll` does not switch the file watcher to polling. The legacy webpack-based karma builder honored both options.

Forward both values to the build options. No new test since both are pass-through options; the package unit tests cover the compilation of the changed setup.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup" (#34654)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`
Issues.Body:
In a Git worktree the development server keeps its Vite cache in the worktree's own cache directory while the configured path resolves to the shared cache of the main checkout. `ng cache clean` removes both since the `getCacheConfig` localPath addition, but `ng cache info` still reports only the shared path and its size, so the cache that the development server actually writes to in that checkout is invisible.

Print the local path and its size when it differs from the shared path. Outside of a worktree both paths are the same and the output is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`" (#34653)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): remove unused exports
Issues.Body: Remove the `export` keyword from four symbols that are only referenced within their defining file: `calculateThresholds` and `checkThresholds`, whose external callers moved to `checkBudgets` in 4d27c38cd4; `augmentAppWithServiceWorkerCore`, which is only called by the exported wrapper functions; and `getEntryPointName`, whose external call sites were removed in 75abe2cc52. The two threshold functions also leave the unsupported `private` entry point, which re-exports the bundle calculator module; neither `@angular-devkit/build-angular` nor `@angular/cli` references them, and both still compile. The public API golden is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(@angular/build): remove unused exports" (#34651)

Issues.Title: docs(@angular/cli): format `[collection:schematic]` as code in generate help
Issues.Body: Wrap `[collection:schematic]` in backticks in the `ng generate` positional argument description so that it renders as inline code rather than an unresolved Markdown link reference in generated documentation.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "docs(@angular/cli): format `[collection:schematic]` as code in generate help" (#34662)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/ssr): remove unused constructUrl helper
Issues.Body: Remove the `constructUrl` function, which was added in 61a027dba7 without a caller and has never been referenced anywhere since. It is not exported from the package entry points and does not appear in the public API golden.

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular-devkit/schematics): remove unused code and exports
Issues.Body: Remove the `FallbackEngineHost` and its supporting types, which have not been referenced anywhere since the devkit repository was merged in 44086c60ff and were never exported from the `tools` entry point, and remove the `export` keyword from four exception classes that are only thrown within their defining file and are not part of the package's public API.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(@angular-devkit/schematics): remove unused code and exports" (#34648)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): explain the latest version fallback when ng add finds no compatible version
Issues.Body: When no version of the package satisfies the peer dependencies of the project, `ng add` reports `Unable to find compatible package.` and then continues to install the version of the `latest` tag. The explanation that the `latest` tag is used was dropped when the command was migrated to the new package manager abstraction, so the installation that follows the message is unexpected.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/cli): explain the latest version fallback when ng add finds no compatible version" (#34650)

Issues.Title: refactor: use ArrayBufferLike.byteLength for schematic dry run event content
Issues.Body: Resolve TypeScript 5.9 TODO comments by using `event.content.byteLength` directly on `ArrayBufferLike` instead of casting through `unknown` to `Buffer`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor: use ArrayBufferLike.byteLength for schematic dry run event content" (#34642)

Issues.Title: refactor: use TEST_TMPDIR in CLI tests, node: imports, and remove unused devDependencies
Issues.Body:
Enforce repository guidelines across packages:
* Use `process.env['TEST_TMPDIR']` instead of `os.tmpdir()` in CLI unit tests.
* Add the `node:` protocol prefix to remaining bare Node.js built-in imports.
* Remove unused package-level `devDependencies` from `@angular-devkit/build-angular`, `@ngtools/webpack`, and `@angular/ssr`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor: use TEST_TMPDIR in CLI tests, node: imports, and remove unused devDependencies" (#34643)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): include builder options for build and test in json-help
Issues.Body:
Allow `ArchitectCommandModule` subclasses to declare multiple builders so that `--json-help` resolves and outputs each builder's schema options separately under the `builders` field.

- Configure `BuildCommandModule` with the `Application` (`@angular/build:application`) and `Library` (`@angular/build:library`) builders.
- Configure `TestCommandModule` with the `Unit-test` (`@angular/build:unit-test`) and `Karma` (`@angular/build:karma`) builders.

See: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71791

**Previews:**
- https://ng-dev-previews-fw--pr-angular-angular-71791-adev-prev-8tejedjq.web.app/cli/test
- https://ng-dev-previews-fw--pr-angular-angular-71791-adev-prev-8tejedjq.web.app/cli/build
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/cli): include builder options for build and test in json-help" (#34644)

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): reuse precomputed hash for in-memory build asset ETags
Issues.Body: Reuse the precomputed `outputFile.hash` on in-memory `ResultFile` entries in `createBuildAssetsMiddleware` instead of recomputing a SHA256 digest on every HTTP request.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "perf(@angular/build): reuse precomputed hash for in-memory build asset ETags" (#34641)

Issues.Title: feat(@schematics/angular): use library builder and add entry-point schematic
Issues.Body:
Updates the `library` schematic to configure `@angular/build:library` with a single `tsconfig.lib.json` and introduces an `entry-point` schematic to generate library entry points under `src/<name>/`.

Closes #19070
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "feat(@schematics/angular): use library builder and add entry-point schematic" (#34645)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular-devkit/build-angular): remove unused picomatch dependency
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the contribution guidelines.
- [ ] Tests for the changes have been added (not applicable: dependency cleanup).
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (not applicable: no user-facing changes).

## PR Type

- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes, no API changes)

## What is the current behavior?

`@angular-devkit/build-angular` declares a direct dependency on `picomatch`, but no longer imports it. Its former proxy configuration consumer moved to `@angular/build` in commit 4ffe07aa24a0fc9ff48461e9c3664d96e92317cf.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

Remove the unused direct dependency, its workspace lockfile entry, and the unused Bazel `@types/picomatch` dependency. Packages that still use `picomatch`, including `@angular/build` and `@angular-devkit/core`, retain their own declarations. This does not claim to remove the transitive package from application installations.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Validation:
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed.
- Prettier and Buildifier checks passed.
- `pnpm bazel test //packages/angular_devkit/build_angular:test //packages/angular_devkit/build_angular:build_angular_dev-server_test --config=no-sharding` passed (both targets). Unit tests: 97 specs, 0 failures. Dev-server: 134 specs, 0 failures, 35 pending.

Issues.Title: feat(material/radio): add compareWith support to mat-radio-group
Issues.Body:
Adds a \compareWith\ input to \MatRadioGroup\ to allow customizing how option values are compared with the selected/form value. This mirrors the behavior in \MatSelect\ when using complex objects as values.

### Changes:
- Added \compareWith\ input property to \MatRadioGroup\ with default to object equality (\===\).
- Added \getMatRadioNonFunctionValueError\ error helper.
- Handled comparison in \_updateSelectedRadioFromValue\ using the custom comparator.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in \adio.spec.ts\ covering value comparison, comparator update, and error throwing.
- Updated documentation in \adio.md\.

Fixes #10495
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "feat(material/radio): add compareWith support to mat-radio-group" (#34092)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): activate the item element on enter and space
Issues.Body: Fixes #34072 The menu's keyboard manager prevents the default action for Enter and Space, and `MenuPattern.trigger()` only called `submit()`. So with the keyboard the item's element was never activated: `` didn't navigate and a `(click)` listener on the item didn't run. Both work with the mouse because the real click happens before the menu handles it. `trigger()` now calls `element.click()` on the active item (when it's enabled and doesn't open a submenu) and then submits, which is the same order a pointer click goes through. The synthetic click bubbles up to the menu's `(click)` host listener, so `onClick` ignores clicks while the item is being activated. Otherwise the item would be submitted twice and focus would jump back into the menu. Items with a submenu still just open the submenu, and disabled items still do nothing. ### Tests - `private/menu/menu.spec.ts`: Enter/Space clicks the element. A click that reaches `onClick` doesn't select twice. No click for disabled or submenu items - `menu/menu.spec.ts`: with the trigger example, Enter on Apple fires one click on the item, emits `itemSelected` once and closes the menu ``` bazel test //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` Without the `menu.ts` change, the two click tests fail (`Expected spy click to have been called once. It was called 0 times.`). ### Manual check I used the reporter's repro (https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro, section B). Its `check.mjs` with the change applied to 22.2.6: ``` B. Enter on → navigates 3/3 as expected B. Enter on

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): close only the focused submenu on escape
Issues.Body: Fixes #34071 Escape inside a nested `ngMenu` was calling `closeAll()`, so the whole menu tree closed and focus jumped back to the trigger. The APG menu pattern says Escape should close the menu that has focus and put focus back on whatever opened it, and that's also how `cdk/menu` and `mat-menu` already behave. I added a `closeCurrent()` on `MenuPattern` and pointed the Escape binding at it. If the menu is a nested submenu (its parent item isn't in a menubar), it closes just that submenu with `refocus: true`, the same path ArrowLeft/`collapse()` already uses. Otherwise it falls back to `closeAll()`, so first-level menus under a trigger or a menubar close exactly as before. ### Tests New specs: - `private/menu/menu.spec.ts`: Escape from a trigger's submenu, and from a nested submenu under a menubar menu - `menu/menu.spec.ts`: directive test using the existing Berries submenu. Escape from Blueberry leaves the main menu open and focuses Berries ``` bazel test //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` I also checked that the new tests fail without the change to `menu.ts` (all three fail with `Expected false to be true.`). ### Manual check I used the repro from the issue (https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro, section A): open menu A, go to Categorize, ArrowRight into the submenu, press Escape. The focused element is outlined in red. Before (22.2.6): both menus close and focus goes back to "Open menu A" After (same build with this change applied): the submenu closes, the root menu stays open and focus is on "Categorize" Ref: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/ (Escape: "Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to the element or context, e.g., menu button or parent menuitem, from which the menu was opened.")

Issues.Title: feat(aria/menu): expose the trigger's tabindex as a public signal on MenuTrigger
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

`MenuTrigger` computes its own tabindex (`0`, or `-1` while its open menu holds the active item) and binds it to the host (`'[attr.tabindex]': '_pattern.tabIndex()'`), but the value is only reachable through the underscored `_pattern`:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/menu/menu-trigger.ts#L45

`Menu` already exposes the same thing publicly (`readonly tabIndex = computed(() => this._pattern.tabIndex())`):
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/menu/menu.ts#L144

The request: add the equivalent `readonly tabIndex` signal to `MenuTrigger`, next to its public `expanded` and `hasPopup`.

### Use Case

A menu trigger inside a roving-tabindex container, such as a keyboard-navigable grid or toolbar not built on `ngToolbar`/`ngGrid`. The container keeps the trigger at `tabindex="-1"` until its cell is active, while the trigger must keep aria's own `-1` while its open menu holds focus. A wrapper directive therefore combines the container's value with the trigger's own, taking the lower of the two.

Today that wrapper has to read `trigger._pattern.tabIndex()`. Deriving it from public state (`expanded() ? -1 : 0`) is wrong while the menu is open but has no active item yet, when aria keeps `0`.

A public `tabIndex` signal would make this composition possible without depending on `_pattern`. An input to let a consumer supply the tabindex would also solve it.

---
_This issue was drafted and filed by Claude Code (an AI coding agent) on behalf of artaommahe._

### [`v12.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.18.0): pnpm 12.18

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.17.0...v12.18.0)

pnpm 12.18.0 packs, publishes, and installs packages with platform variants on pnpr registries. It also adds per-skill approval of agent skills and `pnpm store add` for offline installs from downloaded tarballs. Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer read the `package.json` of unchanged workspace projects. The release fixes several peer dependency resolution bugs too.

##### Minor Changes

##### Agent skills

- pnpm now names the link to a dependency's agent skill after the skill alone. A skill that the `@acme/kit` package ships in `skills/auth/` is linked as `.claude/skills/auth`, not `.claude/skills/pnpm-@acme+kit-auth`. The next install replaces links with the old names. pnpm lists the linked skills in a `# pnpm` block of each agent skill directory's `.gitignore` [#​17455](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/17455).

  When two approved packages ship a skill of the same name, or the name is already taken in an agent skill directory, pnpm links the skill as `pnpm-<package>-<skill>`. Before, the install failed.

- `pnpm approve` now asks which agent skills to link when a package ships more than one. pnpm records the chosen skills as a list, such as `permissions.<pkg>.skills: [guide, migrate]`, and does not offer the other skills for approval again. The first time a project approves a skill, `pnpm approve` also asks which agent directories to link skills into, and records the answer under `skills.dirs`.

- pnpm links agent skills nested in category directories, such as `skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md`, up to three levels below `skills/`. Before, it linked only the skills directly under `skills/`.

##### Platform variants

These features need a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`.

- `pnpm pack` packs one archive per entry of `publishConfig.variants`, each platform variant as `<name>-<version>~<tag>.tgz`. `pnpm pack --variant <target>` packs only the archive whose entry lists that target. `pnpm pack --json` prints the `integrity` and `size` of every archive it writes.

- `pnpm publish` publishes a package's `publishConfig.variants`. pnpm uploads every archive before the publish request that references them. Publishing variants to any other registry is refused unless `--no-variants` is given, which publishes only the archive that targets `any`.

- `pnpm publish --upload-variant <target>` uploads the archive of one `publishConfig.variants` entry to the registry's staging area and prints `<target>=<integrity>`. `pnpm publish --variant-integrity <target>=<integrity>` then publishes the version from archives that other jobs uploaded. With `--recursive`, each value names its package as `<name>~<target>=<integrity>`.

- `pnpm publish -r --batch` now uploads each package archive on its own request and skips archives the registry already holds, so the batch request no longer grows with the archives it publishes. A batch of more than 256 packages still carries every archive inline. Packages with `publishConfig.variants` can be published in a batch. A batch with variants that would reference more than 256 archives on one registry fails with `ERR_PNPM_BATCH_PUBLISH_TOO_MANY_ARCHIVES` [pnpm/tasks#244](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/244).

- `pnpm publish --provenance` signs one statement that names every archive of a version with `publishConfig.variants`. A platform variant's archive is named by the version's package URL with a `variant` qualifier.

- Rerunning `pnpm publish` after the version was already published now succeeds when the published version is the same release. pnpm compares the archives, the provenance statement when the rerun signs one, and the dist-tag. When the published version differs, the publish fails with `ERR_PNPM_PUBLISHED_RELEASE_DIFFERS`, which names what differs.

- pnpm installs the platform variant of a package that fits the host, or the package's own archive when none does. The lockfile records every variant. A version published with variants only, and no archive for other hosts, installs on a host one of the variants fits. On any other host, an optional dependency is skipped, and any other dependency fails with an error that lists the platforms the version is published for.

- `supportedArchitectures` platform lists accept platform tags, the same tags `publishConfig.variants` entries name. An entry can state floors and an ABI, such as `linux-x64-manylinux_2_28`, `darwin-arm64-macos_14_0`, `linux-x64-napi8` or `linux-x64-node127`, and any Node.js OS and CPU, such as `freebsd-x64`. The spellings accepted before still work.

- With `supportedArchitectures` set, pnpm also fetches into the store the variants that the other listed platforms need, when it downloads a package with platform variants.

##### pnpr registries

- pnpm downloads less metadata from a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`. A large package document leaves out the manifests of rarely picked versions, and pnpm fetches one only when it picks that version. In a benchmark that resolves 787 packages, the package documents shrank from 30.3 MB to 2.5 MB gzipped. pnpm caches these documents in `v12/metadata-pnpr`, and the `pnpm cache` commands cover them.

  pnpm warns when a registry that is not declared `serverType: pnpr` turns out to be pnpr. For a registry declared `serverType: pnpr`, a `minimumReleaseAge` longer than 30 days fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE`.

- `pnpm publish` sends release notes to registries declared with `serverType: pnpr`. A package's notes are the section for its version in `CHANGELOG.md`, or the notes that `pnpm version -r` composed from change intents. `--release-notes <file>` gives the notes from a file, and `--no-release-notes` sends none. `--publication-name` names a release published with `--batch`.

  In a workspace that uses pnpm's versioning, `pnpm version -r --release-notes <file>` puts a summary above the composed notes of the release.

  `pnpm view <pkg>@<version> releaseNotes`, `pnpm outdated --notes`, and `pnpm update --interactive` show the release notes from these registries.

##### Store and hooks

- `pnpm store add` now prepares the store for offline installs from package tarballs downloaded some other way. After `pnpm store add ./tarballs/*.tgz`, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` installs each registry package whose lockfile entry pins one of those tarballs [#​2978](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2978).

- Custom pnpmfile fetchers can use `fetchers.gitHostedTarball`, `fetchers.git`, and `fetchers.binary` [pnpm/tasks#191](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191).

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- Running `node` or `pnpm install` in a project that pins a Node.js version pnpm has not downloaded yet no longer hangs when a `globalPnpmfile` is configured [#​17530](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17530).

- `pnpm install` with `enableGlobalVirtualStore` no longer fails on Windows for a dependency from a named registry, such as `gh:` or `npmjs:` [#​17665](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17665).

- Concurrent installs that share a global virtual store no longer fail with `ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_SYMLINK_BIN` when they link the same executable at the same time [#​17587](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17587).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm ci` now succeed when dependency skills are approved but no agent skill directory exists. The skills stay unlinked until a directory exists [#​17574](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17574).

- Commands run from a workspace package now use the same default store as the workspace root. Before, `pnpm add` in a package could fail with `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` when the workspace root was its own mount point and the home store was on another volume, as in a sandbox or a container.

  A workspace installed with the old behavior may need one `pnpm install --force` from the workspace root.

- `pnpm deploy` now keeps a symlink in the project whose target is missing from the source, such as a link into a `node_modules` directory that was removed after the build. Deploy used to drop such a link silently [#​17571](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17571).

- `pnpm install` now links the runtime that an earlier `pnpm install --no-runtime` skipped, and `pnpm install --no-runtime` removes a runtime that an earlier install linked [#​17542](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17542).

- With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, `pnpm install` again runs a dependency's build scripts in a project whose global virtual store slot another project already built, unless the side-effects cache has build output to restore for it. A build that writes only outside its own package, such as a git hook installer, now takes effect in every project [#​17526](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17526).

- Commands of a package whose `bin` paths contain excess parent directory segments, such as `../dist/cli.js`, are no longer missing. Such paths now resolve inside the package [#​17586](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17586).

- Generated POSIX shell shims now quote their paths, so shell special characters in a path stay literal.

##### Lockfile and local paths

- Packages from the default registry keep plain lockfile keys, even when a prefix such as `npmjs` points at the registry set as `registry`. A dependency written with such a prefix shares the plain entry of the same package. The next install rewrites keys that earlier versions qualified this way [#​17575](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17575).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm approve-builds`, and `pnpm rebuild` now accept a lockfile that resolves a `*` dependency to a prerelease `latest` version. pnpm wrote such a lockfile and then reported it as outdated [#​17594](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17594).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts a lockfile written with `excludeLinksFromLockfile` and `linkWorkspacePackages` on, when a project depends on a workspace package through a `catalog:` entry. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer rejects a freshly generated lockfile when `addMissingPeerTypes` is enabled and an injected workspace package has peer dependencies [#​17668](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17668).

- Relative local paths in root `overrides` now resolve from the workspace root when each project has its own lockfile [#​17691](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17691).

  Installing a local directory dependency no longer fails when another project's install is writing a lockfile in that directory.

- Relative local paths in root catalogs now resolve for dependencies and peers [#​17690](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17690).

- `pnpm install` now resolves auto-installed relative `workspace:` and `file:` peers from the directory of the package that declares them [#​17676](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17676), [#​17689](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17689).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` leaves `pnpm-lock.yaml` untouched while it looks for deduplication changes. If `configDependencies` changed since the last install, the check keeps the lockfile they sync, as `pnpm install` does [#​17628](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17628).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is the integrity of a locked version that the registry now reports with a stronger algorithm, such as a `sha512` integrity replacing the `sha1` shasum it reported when the lockfile was written [#​17692](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17692).

##### Peer dependencies

- Peer deduplication no longer gives a project different copies of a dependency across direct and transitive paths when an optional peer has no provider [#​17666](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17666).

- Dependencies no longer bind to another project's peer variant when the provider has nested peers, including providers that finish resolving later [#​17593](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17593).

- Re-resolving a lockfile no longer preserves optional peer bindings from other projects when no provider is in scope [#​17592](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17592).

- `pnpm peers check` warns when a required peer is resolved without a provider declared by the project or its dependency ancestors, with `autoInstallPeers: false` and `dedupePeerDependents: true`. These warnings do not change the command's exit code or cause `strictPeerDependencies` failures.

##### Speed and memory

- `pnpm install`, and `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` with `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, no longer read the `package.json` of workspace projects whose files did not change since the last install. This also holds with a pnpmfile, `configDependencies`, or `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. In an up-to-date workspace with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` no longer runs the install of each project [pnpm/tasks#256](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/256).

- A recursive `pnpm run` or `pnpm exec` with `verifyDepsBeforeRun` set no longer reads every `package.json` in the workspace once per project when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. In a 300-project workspace, `pnpm -r exec true` went from 490 ms to 42 ms [pnpm/tasks#256](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/256).

- `pnpm install` makes fewer `stat` calls when it hardlinks files from the store, as few as 12.7.0 made [#​17543](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17543).

- Picking versions from registry metadata uses less temporary memory.

##### verifyDepsBeforeRun and repeat installs

- With `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now report dependencies as out of date after a dependency is added to the `package.json` of a local directory dependency, such as `"lib": "file:../lib"`. Before, the command ran without the new dependency installed.

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports a `file:` directory dependency as out of date after an edit to `package.json` that leaves its dependencies unchanged [#​17697](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17697).

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as out of sync when only the `version` field of a single-project repository changed [#​17560](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17560). The same holds for a workspace project that no dependency can resolve to. A script run after such a change no longer starts an install first.

- A repeat `pnpm install` now rewrites the bin shims after `extendNodePath` changes. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and the shims kept the `NODE_PATH` of the previous setting.

##### Adding and updating dependencies

- `pnpm add <pkg>` without a version now saves the range that the other workspace projects declare for the package, or the one a matching override sets. A `catalog:` reference still comes first, and the `tag` setting is used only when none of these exists [pnpm/tasks#191](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191).

- `pnpm update` with only negated selectors, such as `pnpm update '!foo'`, now leaves the dependencies listed in `update.ignoreDeps` unchanged. Negated `crate:` and `pypi:` selectors, such as `!crate:sha2`, now exclude that dependency and update the rest [pnpm/tasks#243](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/243).

- `pnpm update --latest` keeps three kinds of Cargo dependencies where they are, unless the crate is named on the command line. Before, it moved each one to the newest release and left a workspace that did not build.

  - A renamed dependency, such as `tower-0-4 = { package = "tower", version = "0.4" }`, stays within its requirement if the workspace also declares the crate under its own name.
  - A crate replaced through `[patch.crates-io]` keeps its version, with a warning.
  - A crate whose newest release is older than its current version, such as a prerelease newer than the latest stable release, keeps its version, with a warning. Only an explicit version, such as `pnpm update crate:foo@1`, moves it back.

  Other new major versions are still selected and may need code changes.

- `pnpm update` now keeps a Cargo dependency at its current version, with a warning, if the new version lacks a feature the workspace enables on it. If the crate is named on the command line, as in `pnpm update --latest crate:sha2`, the update fails with an error that names the missing features.

- `pnpm update` now keeps the operator of every existing Cargo requirement, so `~1.0.0` is updated to `~1.1.0`, and an exact `=` requirement stays exact unless the selector gives a range, such as `crate:foo@^2`. The `savePrefix` and `saveExact` settings apply only to new Cargo dependencies. Saved Cargo requirements omit build metadata.

- `pnpm update` now updates a Cargo dependency whose inline table spans several lines, such as one with a multi-line `features` array. It failed with "its Cargo.toml dependency declaration is not a string or single-line inline table".

- `pnpm update` no longer applies the `savePrefix` and `saveExact` settings to Python requirements. A `savePrefix` such as `^` made `pnpm update` fail in a project with Python dependencies.

  `pnpm update` now keeps the precision of a `~=` requirement, so `~=1.0` is updated to `~=1.5` and still allows any 1.x release. With `--latest`, a `==1.*` requirement is updated to `==2.*`.

##### Store

- `pnpm store prune` now keeps packages linked from a configured modules directory [pnpm/tasks#230](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/230).

- `pnpm store prune` now removes aliases of pruned packages.

- `pnpm store status` no longer reports untouched packages as modified when the global virtual store is enabled. If the installed global-store layout cannot be verified, the command reports `ERR_PNPM_STORE_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE` and asks for a reinstall [#​17631](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17631).

- `pnpm store add` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_STORE_WRITE` when `frozenStore` is enabled. It used to write package files into the read-only store without recording them, so no install could use them.

- `pnpm cat-index <name>@<version>` no longer shows the index of a package whose name differs only in letter case.

##### Other commands and settings

- `pnpm link` now fails without changing `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when the linked package's name is not a valid npm package name. It used to write that name to both files, which made every later install fail [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

- `pnpm link <dir>` now resolves a relative `<dir>` against the current directory. In a directory without a `package.json`, such as a workspace's `packages` folder, `pnpm link .` used to link the nearest project above it into itself [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

- A Node.js version range such as `>=26.13`, for example in `devEngines.runtime`, now resolves to the newest stable release that satisfies it. pnpm picks a prerelease only when no stable release matches [#​17516](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17516).

- Switching to the pnpm version a project pins no longer writes a temporary `_tmp_*` file into the project directory, which file watchers reported on every command [#​17681](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17681).

- pnpm now reads the `linkWorkspacePackages`, `injectWorkspacePackages`, `extendNodePath`, `frozenStore`, and `optimisticRepeatInstall` settings from `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, such as `PNPM_CONFIG_LINK_WORKSPACE_PACKAGES=true`. `--config.extend-node-path` now applies too.

- Recursive scripts run with `--sequential` or `--workspace-concurrency=1` print GitHub Actions log groups again [#​17629](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17629).

- When `pnpm docs` cannot open a browser, the URL it prints no longer includes the query string or the fragment.

### [`v12.17.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.17.0): pnpm 12.17

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.1...v12.17.0)

pnpm 12.17.0 adds `pnpm peers check --global`, dependency-group selectors and wildcards in `overrides`, and runtime, package manager, Cargo, and Python updates in `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update`. It also fixes files that other users could not read in Docker images, and repeat installs that missed changes to local dependencies.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm peers check` now accepts `--global` (`-g`) to check globally installed packages. After a global install or update, the peer dependency warning now suggests `pnpm peers check -g` [#​17504](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17504).

- `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update` now inspect and update package manager and runtime versions in `devEngines.packageManager`, `packageManager`, `devEngines.runtime`, `engines.runtime`, and `runtime:` dependencies. With `cargo.enabled` or `python.enabled`, `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update` also inspect and update Cargo dependencies in `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` and Python dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and `pylock.toml`.

- `overrides` selectors now support `:prod`, `:optional`, and `:peer` pseudo-selectors that target a single dependency group. They also support `*` wildcard patterns on parent and target package names. An override with a non-range value, such as `npm:` or `file:`, no longer adds a peer dependency to `dependencies`. Removing an optional dependency with `"-"` now also removes the duplicate entry from `dependencies` [#​5391](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5391).

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- Files that pnpm creates in a project now get the permissions the umask gives any new file, such as `0644`. Before, several of them were readable only by the user who ran pnpm, which broke Docker images that run as a different user [#​17435](https://redirect.github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17435).

  The fix applies to:

  - `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`. A different user running `pnpm run` reinstalled the dependencies because it could not read this file.
  - `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
  - the files written by `pnpm deploy`
  - patch files from `pnpm patch-commit`
  - the lockfile restored by `pnpm dedupe --check`
  - the Cargo and Python files that pnpm writes

  When pnpm edits an existing file, the file keeps its permissions.

- `pnpm install` no longer writes broken dependency links when the project's `node_modules` is a symlink to another directory, such as another project's `node_modules`. The install reported success, but the links it wrote did not resolve [#​17448](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17448).

- Commands installed with `pnpm add --global` now find the dependencies that pnpm hoists for their package. A package that loads a dependency it does not declare, such as a native addon's platform-specific package, failed with "Cannot find module". Reinstall such a package with `pnpm add --global` to update its existing command [#​17503](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17503).

- When pnpm switches to the version a project pins, it now installs that version's native binary for the current host, even if the project's `supportedArchitectures` excludes the host. Before, pnpm could not use the pinned version and kept running the installed one. pnpm also repairs a pinned version that an earlier install left without the host's binary.

- With the global virtual store, a change to a dependency of one package in a dependency cycle now gives every package in that cycle a new directory. Before, the other packages kept their directories and still linked the old copy of the changed package, so the project could load two copies of it [#​17466](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17466).

  Packages in a dependency cycle, and packages that depend on one, move to new global virtual store directories once after this update. Those that run a build miss the side-effects cache once.

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, when two workspace projects need the same package version and it cannot be hoisted to the root, each project now keeps the copy installed in its own `node_modules`. Build scripts run in each of these copies. Before, the second project's copy was replaced with a symlink to the first project's, so every repeat install imported it again [#​17498](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17498).

- The Node.js `latest` selector now chooses the newest stable release [#​17490](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17490).

- Hardlinking from the store now stats each store file once per install. Since pnpm 12.8.0, a store file was stat'ed again for every package that links it. On an offline install of a large workspace, that added up to 15% system CPU [#​17500](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17500).

##### Repeat installs and local dependencies

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer reports an outdated lockfile right after the install that wrote it. This happened when a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook or `packageExtensions` changed the dependencies or peer dependencies of a local directory dependency outside the workspace projects. It affected a `file:` dependency, an injected `workspace:../dir` dependency outside the workspace patterns, and an injected workspace package left out by `--filter` [#​17447](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17447) [#​17473](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17473).

  A repeat `pnpm install` now takes the fast path when `ignoredOptionalDependencies` removes an optional dependency of a `file:` directory dependency. It used to resolve again on every run.

- `pnpm install` now resolves again after an edit to an injected `workspace:../dir` dependency outside the workspace patterns under a shared lockfile. It used to keep the lockfile unchanged. The next `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` then failed [#​17476](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17476).

- `pnpm install` now resolves a local directory again after its `package.json` changes when an override or a package extension adds it to the dependencies of a registry package. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails on a lockfile that still records the old dependencies of such a directory [#​17486](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17486).

- With `injectWorkspacePackages` and per-project lockfiles, `pnpm install` now updates a project's lockfile when a local tarball that an injected workspace project depends on is replaced. The project's lockfile kept the old version and integrity before.

- `pnpm install` now detects a change to a local tarball or directory that only a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook depends on. A repeat install reported "Already up to date" and kept the old contents before [pnpm/tasks#227](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/227).

- `pnpm install` now relinks a `workspace:` or `link:` dependency whose link was deleted from `node_modules`. It used to report "Already up to date" and leave the link missing [#​17485](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17485).

- A repeat `pnpm install` reports "Already up to date" again when a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook changes the dependencies of a workspace project. Since 12.15.0, every such install ran in full [#​17468](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17468).

  After an edit to a project's `package.json`, `pnpm install` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now run the pnpmfile's `readPackage` hook on the edited manifest before comparing it with the lockfile. They could report the project up to date when the hook rewrote the edited dependency to a specifier the lockfile did not record.

##### Adding and updating dependencies

- `pnpm update --latest` with package selectors now updates the dependencies of the selected packages within their declared ranges. Excluded packages and their dependencies keep their locked versions [#​17444](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17444).

- `pnpm add <pkg>@<tag>` now uses a catalog entry set to that same dist-tag. The dependency is saved as `catalog:` and the entry stays as written [pnpm/tasks#225](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/225).

  When `pnpm add` adds a new dist-tag such as `vue@legacy` to a catalog, the catalog entry records the exact version the tag points to. The same applies to a dependency added without a version when the `tag` setting names a dist-tag other than `latest`.

- `pnpm add` now saves the resolved version range of an npm alias. For example, `pnpm add v2@npm:vue` and `pnpm add v2@npm:vue@^3.0.0` both save `npm:vue@^3.5.13`.

##### Running scripts and commands

- Programs that a script or `pnpm exec` command leaves running, such as a browser opened by the `open` package, now outlive pnpm exactly when they would outlive the command run without pnpm. Before, on Windows, a failed command, `Ctrl+C`, or a closed terminal ended all of them. pnpm still ends them when it is killed or crashes.

  When a recursive or parallel run bails, the scripts still running now receive `SIGTERM` on Unix and are killed only if they are still running two seconds later. On Windows, everything those scripts started is ended, including detached processes whose parent has already exited. Before, a bail killed them at once [#​17465](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17465).

- On Windows, the shell shim of a `.cmd` or `.bat` bin now runs it under Git Bash when MSYS argument conversion is off, such as with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`. The shim used to start an interactive cmd.exe prompt [#​17480](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17480).

- `pnx` and `pnpm create` now run the command in the directory selected by `--dir` or `--workspace-root`. Without either flag, the command still runs in the directory pnpm was started in.

- `pnpm --env-file` now reads files the way `node --env-file` does. Values are taken as written, so `$VAR` is no longer expanded and Windows paths such as `C:\Users\me` load unchanged. A file is no longer rejected for its contents.

##### Settings and messages

- `pnpm version` no longer creates a git commit and tag when `gitTagVersion` is set to `false` [#​17460](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17460).

- `pnpm publish` now reads the `publishBranch` setting from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and from `PNPM_CONFIG_PUBLISH_BRANCH`. The `--publish-branch` flag overrides it.

- `pnpm` now accepts `--strict-ssl` and `--local-address <ip>` on the command line.

- `pnpm doctor` uses a 15-second timeout when checking registry connectivity.

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` parse errors now report `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_SETTING`.

- The error for a dependency with an invalid name in a project's manifest now names the project's directory. It used to say only "The current package", which did not tell which workspace project to fix [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).
