pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v11.28.11`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.11): pnpm 11.28.11 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.10...v11.28.11) pnpm 11.28.11 fixes frozen installs with `excludeLinksFromLockfile`, `pnpm link` in workspaces, `pnpm deploy` with dangling symlinks, and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` starting needless installs. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a symlink in the project whose target is missing from the source, such as a link into a `node_modules` directory that was removed after the build. Deploy used to fail with `ENOENT` on such a link [#​17571](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17571). - A package with `bundledDependencies` and a build script now keeps its bundled dependencies when it is restored from the side-effects cache [#​17523](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17523). - `pnpm install` now links the runtime that an earlier `pnpm install --no-runtime` skipped [#​17542](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17542). - Commands of a package whose `bin` paths contain excess parent directory segments, such as `../dist/cli.js`, are no longer missing. Such paths now resolve inside the package [#​17586](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17586). - Generated POSIX shell shims now quote their paths, so shell special characters in a path stay literal. - A repeat `pnpm install` now rewrites the bin shims after `extendNodePath` changes. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and the shims kept the `NODE_PATH` of the previous setting. ##### Lockfile and resolution - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts the lockfile it wrote with `excludeLinksFromLockfile` and `linkWorkspacePackages` on, when a project depends on a workspace package through a plain version range or a `catalog:` entry. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`. - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm approve-builds`, and `pnpm rebuild` now accept a lockfile that resolves a `*` dependency to a prerelease `latest` version. pnpm wrote such a lockfile and then reported it as outdated [#​17594](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17594). - Packages from the default registry keep plain lockfile keys, even when a prefix such as `npmjs` points at the registry set as `registry`. A dependency written with such a prefix shares the plain entry of the same package. The next install rewrites keys that earlier versions qualified this way [#​17575](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17575). - Relative local paths in root `overrides` now resolve from the workspace root when each project has its own lockfile [#​17691](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17691). Installing a local directory dependency no longer fails when another project's install is writing a lockfile in that directory. - Peer deduplication no longer gives a project different copies of a dependency across direct and transitive paths when an optional peer has no provider [#​17666](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17666). - A Node.js version range such as `>=26.13`, for example in `devEngines.runtime`, now resolves to the newest stable release that satisfies it. pnpm picks a prerelease only when no stable release matches [#​17516](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17516). ##### verifyDepsBeforeRun - With `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now report dependencies as out of date after a dependency is added to the `package.json` of a local directory dependency, such as `"lib": "file:../lib"`. Before, the command ran without the new dependency installed. - `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as out of sync when only the `version` field of a single-project repository changed [#​17560](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17560). The same holds for a workspace project that no dependency can resolve to. A script run after such a change no longer starts an install first. ##### pnpm link - In a workspace, `pnpm link ` now adds the `link:` dependency to the `package.json` of the project where the command runs, not to the workspace root's `package.json`. The link is created in that project's `node_modules`, as documented. The override is still written to the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. - `pnpm link` with several paths now records every linked package in the `overrides` of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Some of them could be missing before. - `pnpm link` now fails without changing `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when the linked package's name is not a valid npm package name. It used to write that name to both files, which made every later install fail [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475). ##### pnpm update - `pnpm update` with only negated selectors, such as `pnpm update '!foo'`, now leaves the dependencies listed in `update.ignoreDeps` unchanged [pnpm/tasks#243](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/243). - `pnpm update --depth 0` without selectors now does nothing when every direct dependency is listed in `update.ignoreDeps`. Before, it failed with `ERR_PNPM_NO_PACKAGE_IN_DEPENDENCIES` [pnpm/tasks#251](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/251). ##### Store and self-update - `pnpm store prune` now keeps packages linked from a configured modules directory [pnpm/tasks#230](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/230). - `pnpm store status` no longer reports untouched packages as modified when the global virtual store is enabled. If the installed global-store layout cannot be verified, the command reports `ERR_PNPM_STORE_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE` and asks for a reinstall [#​17631](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17631). - `pnpm store add` now fails right away with `ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_STORE_WRITE` when `frozenStore` is enabled. It used to retry each download for minutes before failing, or fail with a SQLite error on an empty store. - `pnpm self-update` now reinstalls a cached engine if its executable cannot run. This repairs shared store entries damaged by an earlier install [#​17582](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17582). #### Platinum Sponsors

Packages in a dependency cycle, and packages that depend on one, move to new global virtual store directories once after this update. Those that run a build miss the side-effects cache once. - `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#​17402](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402). - The Node.js `latest` selector now chooses the newest stable release [#​17490](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17490). - The standalone `@pnpm/exe` builds now embed Node.js 26.13.0. ##### Repeat installs and lockfiles - `pnpm install` now resolves a local directory again after its `package.json` changes when an override or a package extension adds it to the dependencies of a registry package. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails on a lockfile that still records the old dependencies of such a directory [#​17486](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17486). - With `injectWorkspacePackages` and per-project lockfiles, `pnpm install` now updates a project's lockfile when a local tarball that an injected workspace project depends on is replaced. The project's lockfile kept the old version and integrity before. - `pnpm install` now detects a change to a local tarball or directory that only a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook depends on. A repeat install reported "Already up to date" and kept the old contents before [pnpm/tasks#227](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/227). - `pnpm install` now relinks a `workspace:` or `link:` dependency whose link was deleted from `node_modules`. It used to report "Already up to date" and leave the link missing [#​17485](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17485). - Merging git branch lockfiles now keeps a workspace project whose directory is named `__proto__`. It was dropped from the merged lockfile before [pnpm/tasks#59](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/59). ##### Adding and publishing packages - `pnpm add` no longer rewrites a catalog entry set to the dist-tag that the dependency resolves through. For example, an entry `beta` stays `beta` after `pnpm add foo@beta` or `pnpm add foo`. Before, the entry was replaced with the version the tag pointed to [pnpm/tasks#225](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/225). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now always include the binary file declared by a string `bin` field in `package.json`, even when `files` or `.npmignore` would otherwise exclude it. - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. It suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. ##### Running commands - Every command, including `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags, now applies the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - On Windows, the shell shim of a `.cmd` or `.bat` bin now runs it under Git Bash when MSYS argument conversion is off, such as with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`. The shim used to start an interactive cmd.exe prompt [#​17480](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17480). - `pnx` and `pnpm create` now run the command in the directory selected by `--dir` or `--workspace-root`. Without either flag, the command still runs in the directory pnpm was started in. - The error for a dependency with an invalid name in a project's manifest now names the project's directory. It used to say only "The current package", which did not tell which workspace project to fix [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475). #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors
### [`v11.28.9`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.9): pnpm 11.28.9 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.8...v11.28.9) This release fixes a crash on registry responses with too many content encodings ([GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c)) and sizes the install worker pool by the container's CPU quota. A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on more setting changes. ##### Patch Changes ##### Crashes and security - A registry response with too many content encodings can no longer crash pnpm. pnpm now uses undici 7.30.1, which fixes [GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c). - `pnpm install` now sizes its worker pool by the CPU quota of the container it runs in, such as a Kubernetes CPU limit, when that quota is smaller than the number of CPUs the container may run on. The default `workspaceConcurrency` respects the quota the same way. On a CI runner with a 4-CPU quota and hundreds of host CPUs, pnpm started hundreds of workers and ran out of memory [#​17382](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17382). ##### Repeat installs and changed settings - A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date". - `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`. - `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories. - `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped. - `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile. - `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail when the `node-linker` setting differs from the one recorded in `node_modules`. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace recreates `node_modules` with the new `node-linker`, and an install filtered to some projects fails [pnpm/tasks#203](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/203). - An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217). - `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm. - `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#​17324](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324). - `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that started the stopped install, such as a patch edit, kept the half-replaced package in `node_modules`. - `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer report the dependencies as out of date after a lockfile change when `dedupePeers` is `true` [#​17322](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17322). ##### Resolving dependencies and the lockfile - A package that a plain range and a `:` specifier both resolve from one registry is now recorded once in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and installed once. The lockfile key names the registry a package resolved from. When that registry declares a prefix, through `prefix` in `registries` or through `namedRegistries`, the package is keyed `@:` however its dependency was written: with the prefix, as a plain range its scope routes to that registry, or through the default registry. Before, the plain range was keyed `@`, so one tarball was installed twice and `instanceof` checks and module singletons broke between the two copies. The same name and version served by two registries still get separate entries. When several prefixes declare one registry, its packages are keyed by the lexicographically smallest prefix. If a scope you route reaches a registry that also declares a prefix, your next `pnpm install` re-keys those entries, which shows up as a lockfile diff. Commit it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded. - `pnpm install` now resolves a scope's packages again when the scope is routed to another registry in `registries`. Before, the lockfile kept the versions and integrity resolved from the old registry, so the install failed when the new registry did not serve a locked version or served different content. pnpm records in the workspace state which registry each scope routed to, so a fresh clone without that record installs the lockfile as recorded. Changing the default registry resolves nothing again, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is unchanged. - An optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix, such as `work:^1.0.0`, now fails the install when it cannot be resolved but the lockfile already has a matching entry from that registry. Such a dependency was skipped, which removed its entries from the lockfile. - With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a `workspace:` dependency written as a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib-a`, in a workspace package now resolves from that package's directory [#​17284](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17284). - Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a workspace package injected through a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib`, has `catalog:` dependencies. Their catalog entries now resolve the way they do for a package injected by name [#​17280](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17280). - `pnpm install` now applies the `serverType` registry setting when it updates the lockfile for an override or catalog change without a full resolution. pnpm wrote the tarball URLs of a declared registry into the lockfile in that case. - Added the `pnpr` value to the `serverType` registry setting. pnpm leaves the tarball URLs of a pnpr registry out of `pnpm-lock.yaml`. - A `registries` entry whose `prefix` is `__proto__` is no longer ignored. - Installs delegated to a pnpr server now resolve every prefix declared for a registry URL. A dependency or lockfile entry that used the second of two prefixes for the same registry, such as `zeta:` next to `work:` in `namedRegistries`, failed on the server [pnpm/tasks#204](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/204). ##### Registries, proxies, and downloading pnpm - The proxy settings `httpProxy`, `httpsProxy`, `noProxy`, `proxy`, and `noproxy` set in the global `config.yaml`, through `PNPM_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY` and the matching variables, or as `--config.httpsProxy` on the command line now apply to `pnpm self-update` and to the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. Previously, these requests read the proxy only from `.npmrc` and the `HTTPS_PROXY` family of variables [pnpm/tasks#215](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/215). - When `https-proxy` is `false`, pnpm now downloads the pnpm version pinned by `packageManager` through the legacy `proxy` setting, as installs already do. Setting `proxy` to `false` now also stops that download from using the `HTTP_PROXY` environment variable. The signature check of the pinned pnpm now uses the same proxy and TLS settings as its download [pnpm/tasks#193](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/193). - `strictSsl` and `localAddress` set in the global `config.yaml`, through `PNPM_CONFIG_STRICT_SSL` and `PNPM_CONFIG_LOCAL_ADDRESS`, or on the command line now apply to `pnpm self-update` and to the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. These requests read them from `.npmrc` only before. `--config.localAddress` now reaches them in the camelCase spelling too [pnpm/tasks#201](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/201). ##### Commands - `pnpm audit --ignore` and `pnpm audit --ignore-unfixable` now exit with a non-zero code when vulnerabilities at or above the audit level remain after ignoring. Before, these commands always exited with code 0. - `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --interactive` now fail with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_FIX_WITH_IGNORE` when combined with `--ignore` or `--ignore-unfixable`. Before, the fix ran and the ignore flags had no effect. - `pnpm ci --lockfile` and `pnpm ci --config.lockfile=true` no longer delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm ci` now always keeps the lockfile and runs a frozen install from it. - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a deployed symlink to a directory inside the project even if the directory is not among the deployed files, such as a link into `node_modules` [#​17288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17288). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` again include the files of a `publishConfig.directory` that is reached through a symlink, together with its bundled dependencies [#​17390](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17390). - `pnpm -r publish --batch` now sends `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/publish`, the batch publish endpoint that pnpr serves. - `pnpm store prune` now keeps the packages that a project still uses when pnpm copied or cloned them into `node_modules`. These include patched packages, built packages, and every package installed with `packageImportMethod: copy`. Before, the prune removed them, and the next install downloaded them again [#​7192](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7192). - `pnpm store prune` now keeps the packages of a project that was installed with a different symlinked spelling of the store path. Previously, prune dropped such a project from its list and removed the packages only that project used from the global virtual store. ##### Speed and output - Sped up installs of projects whose local directory dependencies share transitive local directory dependencies. pnpm no longer checks a shared directory again for each direct dependency that reaches it [#​17374](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17374). - Output that fills the terminal, such as `pnpm run --stream` script output, is now written once. Before, every new line also rewrote all the lines already on screen [#​17387](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17387). - The warning about unrecognized settings now marks `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` as a setting of a newer pnpm version. #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors
### [`v11.28.8`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.8): pnpm 11.28.8 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.7...v11.28.8) ##### Patch Changes - The standalone `@pnpm/exe` builds now embed Node.js 26.12.1. The previously embedded Node.js 26.0.0 still trusted the certificate authority intermediates that Node.js distrusted in October 2026, so a standalone pnpm accepted TLS certificates issued under them. #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors
### [`v11.28.7`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.7): pnpm 11.28.7 [Compare Source](https://redirect.gith > [!IMPORTANT] > ✂ PR body was truncated to here.
--- ### Configuration and setting up pnpm - pnpm now recognizes `externalDependencies` and `autoInstallPeersFromHighestMatch` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` without warning and forwards both settings to `pnpm install`. Previously, setting `externalDependencies` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` crashed `pnpm install` with `externalDependencies.has is not a function` [pnpm/tasks#166](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/166). - pnpm now ignores a `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variable for a URL setting, such as `PNPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, when its value is not a URL. Such a value used to make every command fail with `Invalid URL`. - The warning about unrecognized settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and the global `config.yaml` now names `addMissingPeerTypes`, `autoDedupe`, `bootConfig`, `macosBackup`, `nodePackageMap`, `permissions`, `pipelineBase`, `publishWaitTimeout`, `python`, `remoteCache`, `saveTypes`, `skills`, `storeIndexFormat`, and `tools` as pnpm v12 settings [pnpm/tasks#167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/167). - When a config file has a setting pnpm cannot read, `pnpm --version` now prints the version, and `pmOnFail` and `lockfileDir` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` stay in force. Previously, pnpm switched to the pinned version despite `pmOnFail: ignore`. pnpm also no longer writes the pinned version to `pnpm-lock.yaml` when it cannot read every setting and the running pnpm already matches the pin. - pnpm now records the pinned pnpm version in the `pnpm-lock.yaml` under the `lockfileDir` set in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and resolves a relative `lockfileDir` from the workspace root. pnpm used to write a second `pnpm-lock.yaml` at the workspace root. - `pnpm self-update` now updates the project's pnpm pin when Homebrew installed pnpm or Corepack runs it. The global pnpm is left alone [#​17001](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17001). - `pnpm setup` now completes when Windows registry environment values cannot be read or written. It prints PowerShell commands to configure `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` without registry access [#​17167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17167). - `pnpm setup` now succeeds when it cannot tell which shell configuration file to update, for example in a container where `SHELL` is not set. It installs pnpm and prints the `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` lines to add yourself. Previously it failed with `ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN_SHELL`, and so did the installer script at get.pnpm.io [#​16973](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16973). #### Platinum Sponsors

Issues.Title: fix(material/form-field): support a different direction than the page
Issues.Body:
The form field styles used `[dir='rtl']` selectors, which match any ancestor with `dir="rtl"`. This meant that a form field with `dir="ltr"` inside an RTL page still got the RTL styles: the outline lost its leading border and the label, padding and native select arrow were placed for RTL.

These changes switch the styles to logical properties, so they follow the direction of the form field itself. `transform-origin` and `clip-path` have no logical equivalents, so those two rules use `:dir(rtl)`, which also resolves against the closest element with a `dir` attribute.

Measured in an Angular 22.2 / Material 22.2.6 app (Chromium and Firefox), label offset from the start edge of a `dir="ltr"` field inside a `dir="rtl"` page:

| | Before | After | Plain LTR page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outline | 29px | 16px | 16px |
| Fill | 65px | 52px | 52px |
| Native select | 33px | 16px | 16px |
| Outline leading border | 0px | 1px | 1px |

Fields in a plain RTL page measure the same before and after.

Fixes #26778.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/form-field): support a different direction than the page" (#34081)

Issues.Title: fix(material/list): use theme spacing for leading icons in RTL
Issues.Body:
In RTL, the leading icon of a list item had its margins hardcoded to `32px` and `16px`, instead of using the `leading-icon-start-space` and `leading-icon-end-space` tokens like in LTR. The rule has to use physical properties, because icon font stylesheets (e.g. Material Icons/Symbols) set `direction: ltr` on the icon, which makes the logical margins resolve as LTR inside an RTL list. With the M2 values (16px/32px) this happened to look correct, but with M3 (16px/16px, smaller with density) the gap between the icon and the text was twice as large in RTL.

These changes swap the token values in the RTL rule instead of hardcoding them, so RTL mirrors LTR for any theme.

Measured in an Angular 22.2 / Material 22.2.6 app (Chromium and Firefox), edge → icon / icon → text:

| Tokens | LTR | RTL before | RTL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| M3 default (16/16) | 16 / 16 | 16 / **32** | 16 / 16 |
| M3 density -2 (8/8) | 8 / 8 | **16 / 32** | 8 / 8 |
| M2 (16/32) | 16 / 32 | 16 / 32 | 16 / 32 |

Fixes #30537.

Issues.Title: fix(aria/grid): activate composed widgets when child inputs receive focus
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #34076.

Focusing a child input inside a complex GridCellWidget composed through hostDirectives leaves the widget in cell mode. Add the static ngGridCellWidget host attribute so GridCell._getWidget() can find the containing widget and forward focus events. This follows the static marker approach used in #33839.

Add two tests comparing standard and composed widgets. Both verify that the input receives real DOM focus and the widget activates. The composed case fails before the fix.

[StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-pbfss5v2?file=src%2Fmain.ts): click each input and compare the displayed CELL/WIDGET mode. Detailed steps are in #34076.

This PR is independent of #34075 and addresses widget activation rather than cell selection.

## Validation

- Chromium grid suite passes with the fix (`pnpm test src/aria/grid --no-watch`).
- `pnpm bazelisk test //goldens:aria_api` passes; no public API changes.
- Targeted TSLint, `pnpm ng-dev format changed --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Confirmed the published-package bug with actual mouse clicks in Chrome using the StackBlitz reproduction (Angular 22.2.4, Aria 22.2.6).

Full repository suites and Firefox were not run locally.

Issues.Title: bug(aria/grid): composed cell widgets do not activate when child inputs receive focus
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

A complex GridCellWidget composed through hostDirectives does not enter widget mode when a child input receives focus. The same markup with ngGridCellWidget applied directly works. Focus reaches the input in both cases; the difference is widget activation.

GridCell._getWidget() searches ancestors using [ngGridCellWidget], but this attribute is absent when the directive is composed. As a result, the focusin event is not forwarded to the widget pattern. This concerns widget activation, separately from cell selection in #34074.

Regression status: unknown.

### Reproduction

[Open the minimal StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-pbfss5v2?file=src%2Fmain.ts).

1. Wait for the preview to display “Grid widget child focus”.
2. Click the input under “Standard directive”. Its Mode changes from CELL to WIDGET.
3. Click the input under “Composed host directive”. The input receives focus, but its Mode stays CELL.
4. Compare the two implementations in src/main.ts: both use widgetType="complex" and contain an input; the second applies GridCellWidget through hostDirectives.

The displayed Mode reads GridCellWidget.isActivated(). No synthetic events are needed.

### Expected Behavior

Both widgets should enter WIDGET mode when their child input receives focus, so grid navigation is suspended while interacting with the widget.

### Actual Behavior

The standard widget activates. The composed widget remains in CELL mode even though its child input is focused.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- @angular/aria and @angular/cdk: 22.2.6
- Browser: Chrome
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)

Also reproduced in the repository Chromium grid tests: the standard control passes and the composed case fails.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "bug(aria/grid): composed cell widgets do not activate when child inputs receive focus" (#34076)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/grid): select composed cells when clicking child content
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #34074.

With explicit selection enabled, clicking child content inside a cell composed through `hostDirectives` moves focus but does not select the cell. Clicking the cell host directly works. `Grid._getCell()` searches ancestors using `[ngGridCell]`, but that attribute is absent on composed cells.

Add the static `ngGridCell` host attribute so the existing lookup can find the containing cell. This follows the same approach as #33839 for accordion and adds no signal reads to the grid's host bindings.

Add six regression/control cases covering direct usage, host directives, and inheritance, with clicks on both the host and child content. The tests focus the cell first and verify that the subsequent click changes `aria-selected` from `false` to `true`.

[StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-1z1y55cn?file=src%2Fmain.ts) — blue indicates the active cell; a green outline indicates selection. Detailed mouse-click steps are in #34074.

## Validation

- Before the fix: Chromium grid suite reports **75 passed, 2 failed**, for child clicks on composed and inherited cells.
- After the fix: `pnpm test src/aria/grid --no-watch` passes, **77 specs, 0 failures**.
- `pnpm bazelisk test //goldens:aria_api` passes; no API golden changes.
- TSLint for both changed files, `pnpm ng-dev format changed --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.

Tested locally on macOS arm64 with Node.js 22.23.4 and pnpm 12.16.1. The full repository test suites and Firefox were not run locally.

Issues.Title: bug(aria/grid): clicking child content does not select cells using hostDirectives
Issues.Body: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description When `GridCell` is applied to a reusable component through `hostDirectives`, clicking text inside a child `` moves focus to the cell but does not select it. Clicking the padding on the same cell selects it correctly. The reproduction shows a standard grid and a grid using `hostDirectives` side by side. Both use `enableSelection`, `selectionMode="explicit"`, and `multi`. The standard grid selects cells when clicking either their text or their padding. The reusable cell is defined as follows: ```ts @Component({ selector: 'composed-grid-cell', template: '', hostDirectives: [GridCell], }) class ComposedGridCell {} ``` Its content is ordinary markup, for example `Composed: Second`. This makes the clickable behavior depend on whether the user clicks the text or the surrounding padding. ### Reproduction StackBlitz: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-1z1y55cn?file=src%2Fmain.ts Wait for the preview to load. It uses Angular 22.2.4 and @angular/aria 22.2.6. **Visual indicators:** blue background = active/focused cell; green outline = selected cell. The dashed rectangle marks the child ``; the surrounding padding belongs directly to the cell host. Steps to reproduce with actual mouse clicks: 1. In the first grid, under **Direct ngGridCell**, click the text **Standard: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue and gets a green outline: it is active and selected. 2. In the second grid, under **hostDirectives**, click the text **Composed: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue but gets **no green outline**: focus moves, but selection does not change. 3. Click the padding of that same **Composed: Second** cell, outside its dashed rectangle. A green outline now appears: clicking the host directly selects it. Reload the preview to reset the demonstration. ### Expected Behavior With selection enabled, clicking non-interactive child content inside a cell should select the containing cell, just as clicking the cell host does. Using `GridCell` through `hostDirectives` should behave like direct `ngGridCell` usage. ### Actual Behavior | Usage / click target | Focus moves to second cell | Second cell selected | | --- | --- | --- | | Direct `ngGridCell`: child text | Yes | Yes | | `hostDirectives`: child text | Yes | **No** | | `hostDirectives`: cell padding | Yes | Yes | After clicking **Composed: Second** text, its host has `data-active="true"` but `aria-selected="false"`. Clicking its padding changes `aria-selected` to `"true"`. Possible cause: `Grid._getCell()` searches ancestors with `closest('[ngGridCell]')`, but `GridCell` does not declare that marker as a static host attribute. The marker is present with direct template usage and absent with `hostDirectives`. This report is limited to the cell selection behavior demonstrated above. It does not claim that focus fails to move, or that `GridCellWidget` is affected. ### Environment - Angular: 22.2.4 - Angular CLI / build: 22.2.4 - @angular/aria: 22.2.6 - @angular/cdk: 22.2.6 - TypeScript: 6.0.3 - Browser: Google Chrome - Operating system: macOS (Apple silicon) - Reproduction runs in StackBlitz. Regression status: unknown; an earlier working version has not been identified.

Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Activating a menu item with the keyboard never reaches the item's element:

- `<a ngMenuItem href="...">` (or with `routerLink`) doesn't navigate on Enter.
- A `(click)` handler on `<button ngMenuItem>` doesn't run on Enter.

Clicking either item with the mouse works.

The menu's `KeyboardEventManager` calls `preventDefault()` on handled keys by default (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/behaviors/event-manager/keyboard-event-manager.ts#L34), which cancels the browser's own activation of a link or button. `MenuPattern.submit()` then closes the menu and emits `itemSelected`, but never activates the item itself (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts#L404-L421).

Navigation menus are a common use, and the WAI-ARIA APG navigation menubar example is built from `<a role="menuitem" href>` items that Enter follows. With the current behaviour, routing has to be rebuilt by hand in `itemSelected`, which also loses the href behaviours a link gives (open in new tab, etc.).

A possible fix: have `submit()` call `item.element.click()`. That's what native buttons and links do on Enter, and it makes keyboard and pointer activation run the same path.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/github/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro
Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section B; `node check.mjs` runs the steps with Playwright)
Steps to reproduce:
1. Tab to "Open menu B" and press Enter. Focus is on "Go to #target" (`<a ngMenuItem href="#target">`).
2. Press Enter.
3. Reopen the menu, ArrowDown to "Button with (click)" and press Enter.
4. For comparison, click both items with the mouse.

### Expected Behavior

Step 2 navigates to #target, and step 3 runs the item's (click) handler ("(click) ran" appears in the log), the same as clicking them with the mouse.

### Actual Behavior

In both steps the menu closes and focus returns to the trigger, but the URL doesn't change and the (click) handler never runs. Mouse clicks navigate and run the handler.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (@angular/aria 22.2.6)
- Browser(s): Chromium 156
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

---

Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): Escape inside a submenu closes the whole menu instead of only the submenu
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Escape while focus is in a submenu closes every open menu and moves focus back to the root `ngMenuTrigger`. `MenuPattern` maps Escape to `closeAll()`:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts#L182

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices menu pattern specifies one level: "Escape: Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to the element or context, e.g., menu button or parent menuitem, from which the menu was opened." (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/). The APG navigation menubar example behaves that way.

The other Angular menus already do: `@angular/cdk/menu` closes only the current menu and focuses its parent trigger (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/cdk/menu/menu.ts#L84-L90), and `mat-menu` does the same. So a menu migrated from CDK or Material to `@angular/aria` changes keyboard behaviour.

If closing the whole tree is intended, an option to close one level would help, similar to Base UI's `closeParentOnEsc`.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/github/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro
Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section A; `node check.mjs` runs the steps with Playwright)
Steps to reproduce:
1. Tab to "Open menu A" and press Enter.
2. ArrowDown to "Categorize" and press ArrowRight. The submenu opens with focus on "Mark as important".
3. Press Escape.

### Expected Behavior

Only the submenu closes. Focus returns to "Categorize", and the root menu stays open.

### Actual Behavior

Both menus close and focus returns to the "Open menu A" trigger.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (@angular/aria 22.2.6)
- Browser(s): Chromium 156
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS
